status: DRAFT 19 Oct 2026 (Madhav approved the plan: 'sizing v2 with independent review, sounds solid'); independent review next, then freeze; nothing is run before the freeze
title: Sizing v2: how much of the Rs 60,000 book (and later Rs 2 lakh, Rs 10 lakh and more) an SP1 index decision may use, through which option structure
why: SP1's synthetic option book at 0.25 Kelly paused in April 2017 (-24%) and swung to a 59% drawdown unpaused: a Kelly size on fat-tailed bought-option returns is far too large

at Rs 60,000 one lot is the smallest unit: a Nifty ATM lot (65 x about Rs 70-150) is 7-16% of the book in premium, a Bank Nifty monthly ATM lot (30 x about Rs 400-800) 20-40%; a futures lot needs about Rs 1.5-2.5 lakh of margin, so futures stay in the shadow book

Madhav's rules are fixed: realised plus open loss of 5% of the session's starting equity closes the day; equity 22% below its high-water mark pauses new entries until he resumes; risk per trade is not fixed: it is a research output per situation

evidence_status.seen: every SP1 year 2017 to 16 Oct 2026 has been seen (the SP1 holdout is completed): whatever this study selects is selected on seen data and is EXPLORATORY
evidence_status.synthetic_prices: historical option prices are Black-76 from the previous session's traded IV per strike, held constant through the trade; the option recorder (real 1-minute prices from 21 Sep 2026) calibrates them (R01) before any rupee claim
evidence_status.forward: the selected rule runs in the main paper book from its freeze; the forward checks below decide whether it stays

inputs.decisions: SP1 policy trades exactly as frozen (sp1_v2.json): 2017-2023 from the walk-forward, 2024 to 16 Oct 2026 from the completed holdout run (its own policy_trades), the live paper ledger after that; the sizing never changes which decision is made or when (no fallback to another action)
inputs.prices: for each trade: the index path (entry, exit minute, stop level, stopped), the previous-session chain (expiry nearest strictly after the day, listed strikes, traded IV per strike and type, carry from the forward)

structures.LONG_ATM: buy the call (long view) or put (short view) at the listed strike nearest the index at entry; the current SP1 leg
structures.LONG_OTM1: the same, one listed strike step out of the money (Nifty 50 points, Bank Nifty 100 points)
structures.DEBIT_SPREAD_W: buy the ATM option and sell the same-expiry option W points further out of the money; W in {Nifty: 100, 200; Bank Nifty: 300, 500}; max loss = net debit plus fees, max gain = W minus the debit
structures.pricing: every leg is priced like the SP1 leg (Black-76, its own strike's traded IV, minute-level time to expiry, carry); half-spread max(Rs 0.5 Nifty / Rs 1.0 Bank Nifty, 0.25% of premium) per leg per side, doubled on a stop exit; dated option fees per leg (costs.py v1.1); a sold leg with no traded IV at its strike makes the structure unavailable that day
structures.exits: every structure exits when the SP1 action exits (the index rule decides; T1130, T1515, stops, TRAIL, NEXTOPEN at the next session's 09:16 open); no structure-specific exit

max_loss_per_lot.rule: the planned worst case, known at entry: LONG_ATM and LONG_OTM1 use sp1.loss_per_lot (premium minus the value at the stop moved a further 0.25 daily ATR against the trade at 15:15 with the entry IV, spreads doubled, fees; no-stop exits and NEXTOPEN count the full premium); DEBIT_SPREAD_W counts the net debit plus both legs' entry spreads and fees (its true maximum, any exit)
max_loss_per_lot.check: the realised loss of every trade is compared with its planned max loss; a breach is counted and reported (gap-through-stop days are the expected source for the long structures; a spread cannot breach except by fees)

sizing_rules.FF_f: fixed fraction: lots = floor(f x W_start_of_session / max_loss_per_lot), f in {2%, 3%, 4%, 5%}
sizing_rules.EDGE_f: edge-scaled: f x min(1, z / 2) with z = SP1's pred_net / se for the chosen action (z > c by construction), same f grid
common: W is the book's equity at the session's start (realised; an open NEXTOPEN position marked at the previous close)
the sum of open max losses <= 5% of W (the daily limit is never planned through): a second index's trade the same day gets lots = floor(remaining budget / max loss per lot)
lots = 0 means NO TRADE with the reason counted (size_zero, budget, paused); the book never substitutes another structure or action
lots are integers; contract lot sizes are the dated ones from the F&O files (lots_from_df)
sizing_rules.grid: 2 sizing rules x 4 fractions x 5 structures (LONG_ATM, LONG_OTM1, two spread widths per index treated as SPREAD_NARROW and SPREAD_WIDE) = 40 variants, each run at four starting capitals

capital_tiers.why: the rules are in % of equity so they scale; the integer lot is what changes: at Rs 60,000 many trades are size_zero, at Rs 10 lakh fractions bind; one rule must work across tiers (Madhav: start at Rs 60,000, able to use Rs 10 lakh and more)

survival_simulation.daily_limit: intraday: when realised plus open loss (positions marked at each minute's close from the synthetic prices) reaches 5% of W, everything is closed at that minute and no new entry that day; an overnight NEXTOPEN gap counts against the new session and is checked before D0
survival_simulation.pause: equity 22% below its high-water mark: no new entries; the run records the date and continues as the unpaused path too (both reported)
survival_simulation.paths: the historical path 2017-01-02 to 2026-10-16 from each tier; and 2,000 block-bootstrap paths of 250 sessions (20-session blocks of whole days, trades and their P&L kept together) for the pause probability

metrics_per_variant_and_tier: share of SP1 trades taken, with reasons for the rest
end equity and median one-year log growth (bootstrap)
maximum drawdown (historical), probability of a 22% pause within 250 sessions (bootstrap)
days the 5% limit closed the book; planned-max-loss breaches
P&L by era (monthly-expiry era, weekly era, after the Nov 2024 SEBI rules, after the Apr 2026 STT change)

selection_rule.eligible: a variant is eligible at a tier when its bootstrap probability of a 22% pause within 250 sessions is <= 10% and its historical path never breached the 5% limit by more than fees and gap-through (planned-max-loss breaches <= 2% of trades)
selection_rule.choice: among eligible variants, the highest median one-year log growth at Rs 60,000, provided the same variant is eligible at the other three tiers; ties to the smaller f, then FF before EDGE, then the structure with the smaller max loss per lot
selection_rule.none_eligible: if no variant is eligible at Rs 60,000, the main book does not trade SP1 options (stated plainly); the shadow lines continue; the report shows the smallest capital at which a variant becomes eligible
selection_rule.no_retuning: the grid, the selection rule and the thresholds are fixed by this spec; a variant outside the grid is sz2-v2 and starts its own forward record

forward_checks.record: from the freeze, the main paper book applies the selected variant to SP1's live decisions on real Kite option prices (both legs of a spread from the recorder and the decision-time quotes)
after_60_sessions: execution: realised loss never above the planned max loss by more than 10% on any trade (a breach stops the book for review)

calibration (R01): the synthetic price of the same structure at the same minutes vs the real one; median absolute error and its bias reported; if the bias would have changed the selection, the selection is re-run once on calibrated prices (registered here, not a new choice)
survival: no 5% day missed by the rule; the pause, if hit, stops new entries until Madhav resumes
forward_checks.not_a_profit_test: 60 sessions cannot confirm profitability; profit evidence stays with SP1's index rows and the forward paper record

outputs: paper_config.json main.sizing set to the selected variant (a new cfg version, Madhav's approval)
ledger: one EXPLORATORY row per variant at Rs 60,000 in family SZ (the selection is counted, never claimed as confirmed)
limits: synthetic prices with IV constant through the trade understate volatility crush after rallies and real spreads on big days
a bought option's daily-limit closing uses synthetic minute marks, which can differ from real fills on fast days
the SP1 decisions were themselves selected on these years (seen), so every rupee path here is optimistic
